data, and Python tools to build, train and validate reduced-order models
(ROMs). This page gathers the code associated with my publications, as it
becomes available.

## Research code

Each project below is linked to a publication. Code is released together with
the corresponding article, with examples to reproduce the main results.

::: {.project-card}
[Code available]{.status .status-published}

### Error-aware POD–NN reduction of the shallow-water equations

Non-intrusive ROM combining POD with neural networks that learn both the
reduced coefficients and the projection error. Offline/online workflow, from
high-fidelity snapshots to fast predictions.

[Python]{.tag} [PyTorch]{.tag} [POD]{.tag}

### Wetting-front registration with global volume closure

Transport-aware ROM for moving flood fronts: registration of the wetted area
by dilation, POD–NN compression, and recovery of the front position from
water-volume conservation. Includes large ensemble runs for probabilistic
flood forecasting.

[Python]{.tag} [POD–NN]{.tag} [Registration]{.tag}

[Related article](publications.qmd#submitted-manuscripts){.btn .btn-outline-secondary .btn-sm}
:::

::: {.project-card}
[Code release planned]{.status .status-progress}

### Regime-adaptive local ROMs

Local POD bases, neural-network regressors and a physics-guided classifier
that selects the right local model online, with adaptive model selection.

[Python]{.tag} [Local POD]{.tag} [Classification]{.tag}

[Related article](publications.qmd#manuscripts-in-preparation){.btn .btn-outline-secondary .btn-sm}
:::
